title: Toolchain and developer environment
summary: From empty directory to a machine that can build everything
description:
CURRENT STATE, verified on this machine:
- /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter is EMPTY and NOT a git repository.
- Xcode IS installed at /Applications/Xcode.app, with iOS SDK 26.2 (verified by reading CallKit and IdentityLookup headers from it during design).
- Android SDK is NOT installed — no ~/Library/Android/sdk, no adb, no sdkmanager on PATH. This blocks F001's task T002.
- No Rust toolchain configured for this project.

WORK:
- Install the Android SDK (sdkmanager or Android Studio) with platform-tools and a recent platform. This unblocks T002, which is the highest-risk open question in the project.
- Install Rust and add every target: aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim, x86_64-apple-ios, aarch64-linux-android, armv7-linux-androideabi, x86_64-linux-android, plus host.
- Install cargo-ndk or equivalent for the Android link step, and UniFFI tooling.
- Confirm what free personal-team Apple provisioning permits for APP EXTENSIONS specifically. Known: it runs apps on your own device with 7-day certificates; App Groups require a paid account. F001's harness must be designed to need no App Group. Check this in Xcode's capabilities pane before building anything, not after.
- Write down what a fresh machine needs, then verify it by following it on a clean path. An onboarding doc nobody has executed is fiction.

EDGE CASES: Xcode command-line tools selected correctly (xcode-select -p returns /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer — already verified); Android SDK licences accepted non-interactively for CI; Rust target installs succeeding for the simulator arch matching this Mac.

tasks.title: Install and verify the toolchain
tasks.description:
Get this machine from "nothing installed" to "can build every target". Everything else in the plan is blocked behind this — including P001(F001)/T002, which cannot start because there is no Android SDK.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE OF THIS MACHINE (checked during design, 2026-09-07/08):
- Xcode IS present at /Applications/Xcode.app. `xcode-select -p` returns /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer. iOS SDK 26.2 confirmed at Platforms/iPhoneOS.platform/Developer/SDKs/iPhoneOS.sdk — its CallKit and IdentityLookup headers were read directly to verify the platform constraints recorded across this plan.
- Android SDK is ABSENT. `~/Library/Android/sdk` does not exist; `adb` and `sdkmanager` are not on PATH. THIS IS THE BLOCKER for T002.
- No Rust toolchain configured for this project.
- /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter is empty and is not a git repository (git init belongs to P017, not here).

WORK:
1. Android SDK — install via Android Studio or standalone commandline-tools. Need platform-tools (adb), a recent compileSdk platform, and licences accepted (`sdkmanager --licenses`) so CI can run non-interactively later. Verify `adb version` and that framework sources are readable, since T002 verifies Android claims by READING the framework the same way the iOS side was done.
2. Rust — install via rustup, then add every target the build needs: aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim, x86_64-apple-ios, aarch64-linux-android, armv7-linux-androideabi, x86_64-linux-android. Host target for tests, since F002 is pure logic and must be testable without a device or simulator.
3. cargo-ndk (or equivalent) for the Android link step, and the UniFFI tooling.
4. THE APPLE QUESTION — resolve it here, before anyone builds a harness. There is no paid Apple Developer account. Known: free personal-team provisioning runs apps on your own device with 7-day certificates, and App Groups require a paid account. NOT KNOWN: whether a free personal team can build and run an APP EXTENSION on device at all. This decides whether T001 can proceed. Check Xcode's Signing & Capabilities for an extension target with a personal team selected. If extensions need a paid account, T001 is blocked on purchasing it and that must be reported immediately, not worked around.

EDGE CASES: Xcode command-line tools pointing at the app rather than the standalone CLT (already correct on this machine); Android SDK licences blocking a headless CI run later; the simulator target arch matching this Mac; rustup targets silently failing to install.

DO NOT: create the git repository, project skeletons, or CI here — that is P017. This task ends when every tool is installed and proven to run.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-09-08. Machine can build every target. Every tool verified by running it, not by trusting the installer.

INSTALLED AND VERIFIED:
- Rust 1.96.0 / cargo 1.96.0 / rustup 1.29.0 — ALREADY PRESENT at ~/.cargo/bin, contrary to this task's stated assumption. Only host + wasm32-wasip1 targets were installed.
- Added all six mobile targets: aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim, x86_64-apple-ios, aarch64-linux-android, armv7-linux-androideabi, x86_64-linux-android. Confirmed via `rustup target list --installed`.
- Android SDK installed via `brew install --cask android-commandlinetools` at /opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools. Homebrew and OpenJDK 22 were already present.
- SDK packages: platform-tools (adb 1.0.41 / 37.0.1, runs), platforms;android-36, sources;android-36 (239 MB), build-tools;36.0.0.
- SDK licences accepted (52), so CI can run headless later.
- cargo-ndk 4.1.2 installed and runs.
- Xcode 26.3, macOS 15.7.9, arm64, 399 GB free.

FINDING 1 — sdkmanager needs an explicit --sdk_root. Without it, `sdkmanager "platform-tools"` exits 0 and installs NOTHING. Silent no-op. Every SDK command must pass --sdk_root="$ANDROID_HOME". Also note package naming: the platform is `platforms;android-37.0` (with the .0), while sources are `sources;android-37` — a regex matching `android-[0-9]+` silently truncates the platform name and the install fails with "Failed to find package".

FINDING 2 — UniFFI is NOT a global install. `cargo install uniffi_bindgen` fails: "there is nothing to install in uniffi_bindgen v0.29.5, because it has no binaries". It is a library. The generator is wired into our own crate as a bin target instead — this moves to P018(F008)/T008. User confirmed against https://mozilla.github.io/uniffi-rs/latest/tutorial/Prerequisites.html.

FINDING 3 — ANDROID FRAMEWORK SOURCES ARE READABLE, which unblocks P001(F001)/T002. Verified present in sources/android-36: android/telecom/CallScreeningService.java (682 lines), android/app/role/RoleManager.java (1335), android/provider/BlockedNumberContract.java (649), android/provider/Telephony.java (5208). T002 can now verify Android claims by reading the framework the same way the iOS side was done, rather than from memory. Early confirmation while checking readability: CallScreeningService.CallResponse.Builder does contain setDisallowCall, setRejectCall, setSilenceCall, setSkipCallLog and setSkipNotification — the assumption recorded on F005/R2/P011 holds. (setSilenceCall is declared `public @NonNull Builder setSilenceCall(boolean)`; a grep for `public Builder set` misses it because of the annotation.) Full verification remains T002's job.

FINDING 4 — THE APPLE QUESTION IS ANSWERED: A FREE PERSONAL TEAM CAN SIGN APP EXTENSIONS. P001(F001)/T001 IS UNBLOCKED and the paid account is NOT needed for it.
Verified by building a real throwaway app + Call Directory extension, not by assumption. Evidence:
- Test project generated with xcodegen 2.46.0 (installed for this) at scratchpad/signtest/ — app target plus an app-extension target with NSExtensionPointIdentifier com.apple.callkit.call-directory.
- `xcodebuild -destination generic/platform=iOS -allowProvisioningUpdates DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=UY66NT5LGF build` → ** BUILD SUCCEEDED ** (exit 0), with `CodeSign .../CallDir.appex`.
- Certificate created on demand: "Apple Development: ovidius1972@libero.it (8GT5G9FQ28)".
- TWO provisioning profiles created — one for the app, one for the EXTENSION (com.antoniopantano.signtest.calldir). Apple did not refuse the extension.
- TEAM ID IS UY66NT5LGF. Note the trap: the certificate's own id is 8GT5G9FQ28 and is easy to mistake for the team id; an earlier guess of BJ4HAAB9B3 failed with "No Account for Team".
- Device 00008110-001208843C32801E (the user's iPhone) is in the profile, so it can install.

CONSTRAINTS THIS ESTABLISHES FOR LATER:
- Free-team profiles expire in SEVEN DAYS (created 2026-09-08, expire 2026-09-15). T001's measurement should be done in one sitting; a rebuild re-signs.
- The paid account remains a HARD PREREQUISITE for F004, because the real app needs an App Group to share rules between the host app and its two extensions, and App Groups are unavailable to a free team. Free signing is sufficient for measuring, not for the product.
- The user's iPhone is paired over Wi-Fi, NOT USB. Fine for installing; for T001's memory and timing measurement prefer a cable.
- macOS will prompt for the login-keychain password on first codesign access. Choose "Always Allow" or it prompts every build.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: no git repository, no project skeletons, no CI — those are F008. The scratchpad signtest project is throwaway and its "CallDir" target name carries no decision; real target naming is P018(F008)/T008, where the extension's bundle identifier matters because it is passed to CXCallDirectoryManager.reloadExtensionWithIdentifier:.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE for anyone resuming: ANDROID_HOME and ANDROID_SDK_ROOT are NOT set in the shell profile. Every Android command in this session exported them inline. Setting them persistently belongs to F008's onboarding documentation.

checklist.title: Install Android SDK (platform-tools + a recent platform); verify adb version runs
Accept Android SDK licences so a headless CI run is possible later
Confirm Android framework sources are readable on disk, since T002 verifies by reading them
Install rustup and the Rust toolchain
Add iOS targets: aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim, x86_64-apple-ios
Add Android targets: aarch64-linux-android, armv7-linux-androideabi, x86_64-linux-android
RESOLVE THE APPLE QUESTION: can a free personal team build and run an APP EXTENSION on device? Report immediately if not — it blocks T001
Confirm each tool actually runs, not just that the installer finished
FINDING: uniffi_bindgen 0.29 is a library with no binary — nothing to install globally; wire the generator into the crate as a bin target in T008
BLOCKED ON USER: sign into Xcode with an Apple ID (Xcode > Settings > Accounts). Machine currently has 0 code-signing identities, so no free personal team exists yet
